newsitem.title: CHINA: China warns of jail for bankers dealing in stocks.
newsitem.headline: China warns of jail for bankers dealing in stocks.

text.p: China's economic tsar, Vice Premier Zhu Rongji, got tough with the banks on Thursday, warning that bankers who broke the law to use bank funds to invest in securities could face criminal punishment.
In a speech to bankers attending a nationwide conference called by the central bank, the People's Bank of China, Zhu warned non-financial institutions against engaging in financial business.
A clean-up was to be carried out of all funds, he said in the report carried by the official Xinhua news agency.
In addition no fund was permitted to engage in attracting deposits or extending loans, Zhu said.

The problem of non-bank institutions accepting and loaning funds as well as offering interest rates higher than those set by the banks has become widespread in China in the last few years but many of the enterprises have eluded attempts by authorities to stamp them out.
The banks must get rid of any non-bank financial institutions they have set up, including trust firms and securities companies, Zhu told the meeting.
As for funds held outside official accounts or the use of bank funds to engage in speculation on securities, these must be investigated and exposed, Zhu said.

"As regards those responsible in major cases at banks, they will be sacked and in cases that amount to criminal offences they will be punished in accordance with the law," the Xinhua news agency quoted Zhu as saying. He gave no more details.
